summary: A durable SealedCompiledGraphV1 manifest is required because an in-memory compiled graph is not a content-addressed artifact.
The seal binds bodies, typed arguments, effective writes, routing, schemas, compiler inputs, policies, gates, effects, and the admission proof in addition to topology.
Frozen registry membership is insufficient; each executable body and factory contract requires immutable artifact identity or trusted-boundary execution.
Artifact integrity never implies current authority; policy, epoch, approval, budget, head, resource version, lease, fence, and effect permission stay live.
Durable human approval binds the sealed consequence and full live dependency vector and remains evidence rather than a bearer capability.
Declared writes plan authorization and locking, while only mutation-side fence and head/version revalidation authorize commit.
Governance mutants must cover seal-content swaps and live-authority staleness, failing at the earliest owning boundary with zero unauthorized mutation.
